prerequisites: Calculation, Design and Testing of Machines (596)

learning_outcomes.text: Know the graphic representation standards for different mechanical elements and manufacturing processes.
Correctly interpret drawings, studying parts and assemblies and discerning the function of each component.
Graphically solve problems that arise in the execution of mechanical projects.
Demonstrate the importance of dimensional and formal quality for both manufacturing and product function.
Skillfully use the most advanced techniques of graphic expression in the representation of three-dimensional assemblies.
Produce drawings for any industrial mechanical project.

syllabus_topics: MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 1. Dimensioning for manufacturing and verification: The design process and concurrent engineering. Forming manufacturing. Material removal manufacturing. Criteria for dimension selection.
MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 2. Material Selection: Technological applications, ecodesign and life cycle analysis.
MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 3. Dimensional tolerances: Fundamentals. Fits. General tolerances. Tolerance verification. Regulations. Applications.

MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 4. Geometric tolerances: Fundamentals. References. Symbols. Interpretation. General tolerances. Relationship between dimensional and geometric tolerances. Regulations. Applications.
MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 5. Functional analysis: Dimension chains. Analysis with geometric tolerances. Statistical tolerances. Dimension transfer.
MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 6. Surface states: Surface irregularities. Symbols. Surface quality. Surface states and manufacturing processes. Regulations. Applications.
MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 7. Fixed joints: Welded joints. Riveted joints. Glued and adhesive joints. Regulations. Applications.

MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 8. Removable joints: Threaded joints (profiles, screws, nuts, washers, safety or locking systems, qualities, tightening torque). Springs. Clamps. Regulations. Applications.

MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 9. Motion transmission mechanisms: Shafts and axles. Keys and splines. Circular-rectilinear motion transmission. Circular-circular motion transmission. Applications.

MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 10. Supports and contact components between transmission mechanisms: Antifriction bearings. Rolling bearings. (Function, types, selection criteria, dimensions, assembly/disassembly, fixings, tolerances and fits). Lubrication systems (greasers, channels, seals). Applications.
MODULE 1: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION - 11. Gears, chains and belts: Fundamentals. Gears (types, representation, tolerances and fits). Chains. Pulleys. Cables. Belts. Applications.
MODULE 2: COMPUTER GRAPHICS TECHNIQUES - 12. Surface modeling. Solid modeling.
MODULE 2: COMPUTER GRAPHICS TECHNIQUES - 14. Assembly design. Constraints.
MODULE 2: COMPUTER GRAPHICS TECHNIQUES - 15. Visualization: textures, lighting, animation.
MODULE 2: COMPUTER GRAPHICS TECHNIQUES - 16. Part drawing editing. Printing and file management.

PRACTICE module 1: Freehand design of a mechanical device containing components studied in topics 7 to 11. Assembly drawings, bill of materials, part drawings, dimensioning with dimensional and geometric tolerances, surface qualities.

PRACTICE module 2: CAD program design of the device developed in module 1 practice: 3D assembly with motion constraints; 2D part drawings (dimensioned with dimensional and geometric tolerances). Import of commercial components from free-use databases.
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, the student must achieve at least 25% in written tests and 50% in the sum of all evaluation systems. If this critical evaluation criterion is not met, the total grade for the subject will be FAIL, with the resulting grade from the sum of the qualifications obtained in all evaluation systems, truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points. Students with recognized part-time study dedication may substitute non-recoverable activities with similar ones or equivalent assessment tests if the reason for non-completion is due to part-time status.
